title: Design a Rate Limiter
description: An API's 60-per-minute fixed-window limit admits 60 calls at 12:00:59 and another 60 at 12:01:01. The team is comparing alternatives. Which explanation accounts for what happened?

options.text: Fixed window counter resets at fixed intervals and can allow 2x the rate at window boundaries
options.explanation: Fixed window counters reset at interval boundaries. A burst at the end of one window and start of the next can allow double the intended rate.

options.text: Token bucket cannot handle burst traffic
options.explanation: Token bucket explicitly supports burst traffic — tokens accumulate up to a max bucket size, allowing short bursts.

options.text: Sliding window log is the most memory-efficient algorithm
options.explanation: A sliding log stores timestamps across the trailing window, so memory grows with request volume. A sliding counter uses much smaller state but approximates the boundary.

options.text: Leaky bucket processes requests at a variable rate
options.explanation: A leaky-bucket queue drains accepted work at a fixed configured rate. Bursts create queueing delay, so the queue needs a bound.
